497	/-! ## The class law: the datum class is the pulled fiber twist -/
498	
499	section ClassLaw
500	
501	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
502	variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π]
503	variable [IsIntegral C.left] [IsIntegral (relCurve C k)]
504	variable (a : ℕ)
505	
506	omit [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π] in
507	/-- The base-field collapse maps the generic point to the generic point. -/
508	lemma fst_left_self_genericPoint :
509	    ((fst C (overSpec k k)).left).base (genericPoint (relCurve C k))
510	      = genericPoint C.left := by
511	  haveI : IrreducibleSpace (↥(C ⊗ overSpec k k).left) :=
512	    (inferInstance : IrreducibleSpace (↥(relCurve C k)))
513	  exact genericPoint_eq_of_surjective _
514	
515	/-- **The pulled fiber system**: the local-equation system of `a · F` on `C.left`,
516	pulled back along the base-field collapse — regularity for free from integrality. -/
517	noncomputable def thetaFiberPullback : (relCurve C k).LocalEquations :=
518	  haveI : IsIntegral (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left := ‹IsIntegral (relCurve C k)›
519	  (fiberDivisor π a).pullback (fst C (overSpec k k)).left
520	    (fun y z hz => Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn_germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors
521	      (fst C (overSpec k k)).left (fst_left_self_genericPoint C) (fiberDivisor π a) y z hz)
522	
523	omit [IsFinite π] in
524	/-- The pulled fiber system presents the pulled fiber twist `Θᵃ`. -/
525	lemma thetaFiberPullback_picClass :
526	    (thetaFiberPullback C π a).picClass
527	      = Scheme.CechPic.map (fst C (overSpec k k)).left (fiberTwist π a) :=
528	  Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_pullback _ _ _
529	
530	omit [IsFinite π] in
531	/-- The transition units of the pulled fiber system are the pulled transition units. -/
532	lemma thetaFiberPullback_ratioUnit (z w : relCurve C k) :
533	    (thetaFiberPullback C π a).ratioUnit z w
534	      = (fst C (overSpec k k)).left.unitsAppLE
535	          ((fiberCover π).opens (((fst C (overSpec k k)).left).base z)
536	            ⊓ (fiberCover π).opens (((fst C (overSpec k k)).left).base w))
537	          (((fiberCover π).pullback (fst C (overSpec k k)).left).opens z
538	            ⊓ ((fiberCover π).pullback (fst C (overSpec k k)).left).opens w)
539	          ((fst C (overSpec k k)).left.le_preimage_inf inf_le_left inf_le_right)
540	          ((fiberDivisor π a).ratioUnit (((fst C (overSpec k k)).left).base z)
541	            (((fst C (overSpec k k)).left).base w)) :=
542	  Scheme.LocalEquations.pullback_ratioUnit _ _ _ z w
543	
544	omit [IsFinite π] in
545	/-- The pulled-system pair values in ratio-unit form. -/
546	lemma thetaFiberPullback_evInf (z w : relCurve C k) :
547	    Scheme.unitsEvInf (thetaFiberPullback C π a).unitsCocycle z w
548	      = (thetaFiberPullback C π a).ratioUnit z w :=
549	  (thetaFiberPullback C π a).unitsCocycle_evInf z w
550	
551	/-! ### The chart classification -/
552	
553	open Classical in
554	/-- The chart classification of a point of the relative curve: chart 0 if its image
555	lies in the first pinned chart, chart 1 otherwise. -/
556	noncomputable def thetaChartIndex (z : relCurve C k) : (thetaChartCover C k π).index :=
557	  if ((fst C (overSpec k k)).left).base z ∈ fiberChart₀ π then Sum.inl PUnit.unit
558	  else Sum.inr PUnit.unit
559	
560	omit [IsDominant π] [IsIntegral C.left] [IsIntegral (relCurve C k)] in
561	lemma thetaChartIndex_of_mem {z : relCurve C k}
562	    (h : ((fst C (overSpec k k)).left).base z ∈ fiberChart₀ π) :
563	    thetaChartIndex C π z = Sum.inl PUnit.unit := if_pos h
564	
565	omit [IsDominant π] [IsIntegral C.left] [IsIntegral (relCurve C k)] in
566	lemma thetaChartIndex_of_notMem {z : relCurve C k}
567	    (h : ((fst C (overSpec k k)).left).base z ∉ fiberChart₀ π) :
568	    thetaChartIndex C π z = Sum.inr PUnit.unit := if_neg h
569	
570	omit [IsDominant π] [IsIntegral C.left] [IsIntegral (relCurve C k)] in
571	/-- The pulled fiber cover is subordinated to the whole-chart pieces along the chart
572	classification. -/
573	lemma pullback_fiberCover_le_pieces (z : relCurve C k) :
574	    ((fiberCover π).pullback (fst C (overSpec k k)).left).opens z
575	      ≤ (thetaChartCover C k π).pieces (thetaChartIndex C π z) := by
576	  by_cases h : ((fst C (overSpec k k)).left).base z ∈ fiberChart₀ π
577	  · rw [thetaChartIndex_of_mem C π h, thetaChartCover_pieces_inl,
578	      Scheme.PointedCover.pullback_opens, fiberCover_opens_of_mem π h]
579	    exact le_rfl
580	  · rw [thetaChartIndex_of_notMem C π h, thetaChartCover_pieces_inr,
581	      Scheme.PointedCover.pullback_opens, fiberCover_opens_of_notMem π h]
582	    exact le_rfl
583	
584	/-! ### Value normal forms -/
585	
586	omit [IsDominant π] [IsIntegral C.left] [IsIntegral (relCurve C k)] in
587	/-- The subordinated pair value at known chart indices, in `resHom` normal form. -/
588	private lemma gluedSubordUnit_val_of_eq {z w : relCurve C k}
589	    {i j : (thetaChartCover C k π).index} (hi : thetaChartIndex C π z = i)
590	    (hj : thetaChartIndex C π w = j)
591	    (hle : ((fiberCover π).pullback (fst C (overSpec k k)).left).opens z
592	        ⊓ ((fiberCover π).pullback (fst C (overSpec k k)).left).opens w
593	      ≤ (thetaChartCover C k π).pieces i ⊓ (thetaChartCover C k π).pieces j) :
594	    (gluedSubordUnit (thetaChartDatum C k π a).unit
595	        ((fiberCover π).pullback (fst C (overSpec k k)).left) (thetaChartIndex C π)
596	        (pullback_fiberCover_le_pieces C π) z w
597	      : Γ(relCurve C k, ((fiberCover π).pullback (fst C (overSpec k k)).left).opens z
598	          ⊓ ((fiberCover π).pullback (fst C (overSpec k k)).left).opens w))
599	      = (relCurve C k).resHom hle
600	          (thetaChartUnit C k π a i j
601	            : Γ(relCurve C k, (thetaChartCover C k π).pieces i
602	                ⊓ (thetaChartCover C k π).pieces j)) := by
603	  subst hi
604	  subst hj
605	  rfl
606	
607	omit [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π] [IsIntegral C.left] [IsIntegral (relCurve C k)] in
608	/-- Restriction after `appLE` composes to a single `appLE` (elementwise). -/
609	private lemma resHom_appLE_apply {U : C.left.Opens} {V V' : (relCurve C k).Opens}
610	    (e : V ≤ (fst C (overSpec k k)).left ⁻¹ᵁ U) (h : V' ≤ V) (s : Γ(C.left, U)) :
611	    (relCurve C k).resHom h (((fst C (overSpec k k)).left.appLE U V e).hom s)
612	      = ((fst C (overSpec k k)).left.appLE U V' (h.trans e)).hom s := by
613	  have hcomp : (fst C (overSpec k k)).left.appLE U V e
614	        ≫ (relCurve C k).presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op
615	      = (fst C (overSpec k k)).left.appLE U V' (h.trans e) :=
616	    Scheme.Hom.appLE_map (fst C (overSpec k k)).left e (homOfLE h).op
617	  exact congr($(hcomp).hom s)
618	
619	omit [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π] [IsIntegral C.left] [IsIntegral (relCurve C k)] in
620	/-- `appLE` after restriction composes to a single `appLE` (elementwise). -/
621	private lemma appLE_resHom_apply {U' U : C.left.Opens} {V : (relCurve C k).Opens}
622	    (h : U' ≤ U) (e : V ≤ (fst C (overSpec k k)).left ⁻¹ᵁ U') (s : Γ(C.left, U)) :
623	    ((fst C (overSpec k k)).left.appLE U' V e).hom (C.left.resHom h s)
624	      = ((fst C (overSpec k k)).left.appLE U V
625	          (e.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_mono (fst C (overSpec k k)).left h))).hom s := by
626	  have hcomp : C.left.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op
627	        ≫ (fst C (overSpec k k)).left.appLE U' V e
628	      = (fst C (overSpec k k)).left.appLE U V
629	          (e.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_mono (fst C (overSpec k k)).left h)) :=
630	    Scheme.Hom.map_appLE (fst C (overSpec k k)).left e (homOfLE h).op
631	  exact congr($(hcomp).hom s)
632	
633	omit [IsDominant π] [IsIntegral C.left] [IsIntegral (relCurve C k)] in
634	/-- The relative theta cocycle value is the collapse image of the theta power. -/
635	private lemma relThetaCocycle_val' :
636	    ((relThetaCocycle C k π a
637	        : Γ(relCurve C k, (relCover C k (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
638	            ⊓ (relCover C k (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)ˣ)
639	      : Γ(relCurve C k, (relCover C k (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
640	          ⊓ (relCover C k (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁))
641	      = ((fst C (overSpec k k)).left.appLE (fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)
642	          ((relCover C k (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓ (relCover C k (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
643	          (le_of_eq (relCover_inf C k (fiberTwoCover π)))).hom
644	        ((thetaUnit π ^ a : Γ(C.left, fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)ˣ)
645	          : Γ(C.left, fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)) := rfl
646	
647	omit [IsDominant π] [IsIntegral C.left] [IsIntegral (relCurve C k)] in
648	/-- The inverse relative theta cocycle value is the collapse image of the inverse. -/
649	private lemma relThetaCocycle_inv_val' :
650	    (((relThetaCocycle C k π a)⁻¹
651	        : Γ(relCurve C k, (relCover C k (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
652	            ⊓ (relCover C k (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)ˣ)
653	      : Γ(relCurve C k, (relCover C k (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
654	          ⊓ (relCover C k (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁))
655	      = ((fst C (overSpec k k)).left.appLE (fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)
656	          ((relCover C k (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓ (relCover C k (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
657	          (le_of_eq (relCover_inf C k (fiberTwoCover π)))).hom
658	        (((thetaUnit π ^ a)⁻¹ : Γ(C.left, fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)ˣ)
659	          : Γ(C.left, fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)) := rfl
660	
661	/-! ### The class law -/
662	
663	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
664	-- (The four-branch unit comparison crosses the `relCurve`/product spelling seam
665	-- repeatedly; the defeq checks exceed the default limit.)
666	/-- **The class law**: the Čech Picard class of the whole-chart theta datum is the
667	pullback of the fiber twist `Θᵃ` along the base-field collapse. -/
668	theorem cechPicClass_thetaChartDatum :
669	    (thetaChartDatum C k π a).cechPicClass
670	      = Scheme.CechPic.map (fst C (overSpec k k)).left (fiberTwist π a) := by
671	  rw [← thetaFiberPullback_picClass C π a,
672	    ← (thetaChartDatum C k π a).cechPicClass_eq_mk
673	      ((fiberCover π).pullback (fst C (overSpec k k)).left) (thetaChartIndex C π)
674	      (pullback_fiberCover_le_pieces C π)]
675	  have hR : (thetaFiberPullback C π a).picClass
676	      = Scheme.CechPic.mk ((fiberCover π).pullback (fst C (overSpec k k)).left)
677	          (thetaFiberPullback C π a).unitsCocycle.class := rfl
678	  rw [hR]
679	  refine congrArg (fun γ : (relCurve C k).unitsCocycle _ =>
680	    Scheme.CechPic.mk ((fiberCover π).pullback (fst C (overSpec k k)).left) γ.class)
681	    (Scheme.unitsCocycle_ext fun z w => ?_)
682	  rw [gluedSubordCocycle_evInf, thetaFiberPullback_evInf,
683	    thetaFiberPullback_ratioUnit]
684	  by_cases hz : ((fst C (overSpec k k)).left).base z ∈ fiberChart₀ π <;>
685	    by_cases hw : ((fst C (overSpec k k)).left).base w ∈ fiberChart₀ π
686	  · -- both chart 0: both units are `1`
687	    rw [fiberDivisor_ratioUnit_mem_mem π a hz hw, map_one]
688	    refine Units.ext ?_
689	    rw [gluedSubordUnit_val_of_eq C π a (thetaChartIndex_of_mem C π hz)
690	      (thetaChartIndex_of_mem C π hw)
691	      (inf_le_inf ((thetaChartIndex_of_mem C π hz) ▸ pullback_fiberCover_le_pieces C π z)
692	        ((thetaChartIndex_of_mem C π hw) ▸ pullback_fiberCover_le_pieces C π w))]
693	    have hu : thetaChartUnit C k π a (Sum.inl PUnit.unit) (Sum.inl PUnit.unit) = 1 := rfl
694	    rw [hu, Units.val_one, map_one, Units.val_one]
695	  · -- chart 0 to chart 1: the theta power
696	    rw [fiberDivisor_ratioUnit_mem_notMem π a hz hw]
697	    refine Units.ext ?_
698	    rw [gluedSubordUnit_val_of_eq C π a (thetaChartIndex_of_mem C π hz)
699	      (thetaChartIndex_of_notMem C π hw)
700	      (inf_le_inf ((thetaChartIndex_of_mem C π hz) ▸ pullback_fiberCover_le_pieces C π z)
701	        ((thetaChartIndex_of_notMem C π hw) ▸ pullback_fiberCover_le_pieces C π w))]
702	    have hval : (thetaChartUnit C k π a (Sum.inl PUnit.unit) (Sum.inr PUnit.unit)
703	          : Γ(relCurve C k, (thetaChartCover C k π).pieces (Sum.inl PUnit.unit)
704	              ⊓ (thetaChartCover C k π).pieces (Sum.inr PUnit.unit)))
705	        = (relCurve C k).resHom
706	            (inf_le_inf (thetaChartCover_pieces_le_inl C k π PUnit.unit)
707	              (thetaChartCover_pieces_le_inr C k π PUnit.unit))
708	            ((relThetaCocycle C k π a
709	                : Γ(relCurve C k, (relCover C k (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
710	                    ⊓ (relCover C k (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)ˣ)
711	              : Γ(relCurve C k, _)) := rfl
712	    rw [hval, Scheme.resHom_resHom, relThetaCocycle_val', resHom_appLE_apply]
713	    have hRval : ((fst C (overSpec k k)).left.unitsAppLE
714	          ((fiberCover π).opens (((fst C (overSpec k k)).left).base z)
715	              ⊓ (fiberCover π).opens (((fst C (overSpec k k)).left).base w))
716	          (((fiberCover π).pullback (fst C (overSpec k k)).left).opens z
717	              ⊓ ((fiberCover π).pullback (fst C (overSpec k k)).left).opens w)
718	          ((fst C (overSpec k k)).left.le_preimage_inf inf_le_left inf_le_right)
719	          (C.left.unitsRestrict (opens_inf_le_of_mem_of_notMem π hz hw)
720	            (thetaUnit π ^ a))).val
721	        = ((fst C (overSpec k k)).left.appLE
722	            ((fiberCover π).opens (((fst C (overSpec k k)).left).base z)
723	              ⊓ (fiberCover π).opens (((fst C (overSpec k k)).left).base w))
724	            (((fiberCover π).pullback (fst C (overSpec k k)).left).opens z
725	              ⊓ ((fiberCover π).pullback (fst C (overSpec k k)).left).opens w)
726	            ((fst C (overSpec k k)).left.le_preimage_inf inf_le_left inf_le_right)).hom
727	          (C.left.resHom (opens_inf_le_of_mem_of_notMem π hz hw)
728	            ((thetaUnit π ^ a : Γ(C.left, fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)ˣ)
729	              : Γ(C.left, fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π))) := rfl
730	    rw [hRval, appLE_resHom_apply]
731	  · -- chart 1 to chart 0: the inverse theta power
732	    rw [fiberDivisor_ratioUnit_notMem_mem π a hz hw]
733	    refine Units.ext ?_
734	    rw [gluedSubordUnit_val_of_eq C π a (thetaChartIndex_of_notMem C π hz)
735	      (thetaChartIndex_of_mem C π hw)
736	      (inf_le_inf ((thetaChartIndex_of_notMem C π hz) ▸ pullback_fiberCover_le_pieces C π z)
737	        ((thetaChartIndex_of_mem C π hw) ▸ pullback_fiberCover_le_pieces C π w))]
738	    have hval : (thetaChartUnit C k π a (Sum.inr PUnit.unit) (Sum.inl PUnit.unit)
739	          : Γ(relCurve C k, (thetaChartCover C k π).pieces (Sum.inr PUnit.unit)
740	              ⊓ (thetaChartCover C k π).pieces (Sum.inl PUnit.unit)))
741	        = (relCurve C k).resHom
742	            (le_inf (inf_le_right.trans (thetaChartCover_pieces_le_inl C k π PUnit.unit))
743	              (inf_le_left.trans (thetaChartCover_pieces_le_inr C k π PUnit.unit)))
744	            (((relThetaCocycle C k π a)⁻¹
745	                : Γ(relCurve C k, (relCover C k (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
746	                    ⊓ (relCover C k (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)ˣ)
747	              : Γ(relCurve C k, _)) := rfl
748	    rw [hval, Scheme.resHom_resHom, relThetaCocycle_inv_val', resHom_appLE_apply]
749	    have hRval : ((fst C (overSpec k k)).left.unitsAppLE
750	          ((fiberCover π).opens (((fst C (overSpec k k)).left).base z)
751	              ⊓ (fiberCover π).opens (((fst C (overSpec k k)).left).base w))
752	          (((fiberCover π).pullback (fst C (overSpec k k)).left).opens z
753	              ⊓ ((fiberCover π).pullback (fst C (overSpec k k)).left).opens w)
754	          ((fst C (overSpec k k)).left.le_preimage_inf inf_le_left inf_le_right)
755	          (C.left.unitsRestrict (opens_inf_le_of_notMem_of_mem π hz hw)
756	            (thetaUnit π ^ a)⁻¹)).val
757	        = ((fst C (overSpec k k)).left.appLE
758	            ((fiberCover π).opens (((fst C (overSpec k k)).left).base z)
759	              ⊓ (fiberCover π).opens (((fst C (overSpec k k)).left).base w))
760	            (((fiberCover π).pullback (fst C (overSpec k k)).left).opens z
761	              ⊓ ((fiberCover π).pullback (fst C (overSpec k k)).left).opens w)
762	            ((fst C (overSpec k k)).left.le_preimage_inf inf_le_left inf_le_right)).hom
763	          (C.left.resHom (opens_inf_le_of_notMem_of_mem π hz hw)
764	            (((thetaUnit π ^ a)⁻¹ : Γ(C.left, fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)ˣ)
765	              : Γ(C.left, fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π))) := rfl
766	    rw [hRval, appLE_resHom_apply]
767	  · -- both chart 1: both units are `1`
768	    rw [fiberDivisor_ratioUnit_notMem_notMem π a hz hw, map_one]
769	    refine Units.ext ?_
770	    rw [gluedSubordUnit_val_of_eq C π a (thetaChartIndex_of_notMem C π hz)
771	      (thetaChartIndex_of_notMem C π hw)
772	      (inf_le_inf ((thetaChartIndex_of_notMem C π hz) ▸ pullback_fiberCover_le_pieces C π z)
773	        ((thetaChartIndex_of_notMem C π hw) ▸ pullback_fiberCover_le_pieces C π w))]
774	    have hu : thetaChartUnit C k π a (Sum.inr PUnit.unit) (Sum.inr PUnit.unit) = 1 := rfl
775	    rw [hu, Units.val_one, map_one, Units.val_one]
776	
777	end ClassLaw
778	
779	end AlgebraicGeometry

1	/-

4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.TwoChartCechPicTrivial
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.LaurentUnits
8	
9	/-!
10	# THE ℙ¹ TWO-CHART COBOUNDARY SUBGROUP OVER A DOMAIN IS EXACTLY THE CONSTANTS
11	
12	`Picard/TwoChartCechPicTrivial.lean` reduces triviality of a chart-trivial Picard class on a
13	two-chart cover to the purely algebraic question *are the overlap units all coboundaries?*.  This
14	file answers that question for the pinned ℙ¹ chart data — overlap ring `A[t,t⁻¹]`, chart rings
15	`A[t]` and `A[t⁻¹]` — over a **domain** `A`, in both directions:
16	
17	> a Laurent unit is a coboundary **iff** it is `C c` for a unit `c` of `A`.
18	
19	## Read this before using it: the answer is NO, and that is the correct answer
20	
21	The criterion of the previous file asks for *every* overlap unit to be a coboundary.  Over a
22	domain that is **false**, and this file is what proves it false: `T 1 = t` is a unit of
23	`A[t,t⁻¹]` and is *not* a coboundary, because `t` is a unit of neither chart ring
24	(`Polynomial.isUnit_iff`: a unit of `A[t]` over a domain is a constant).
25	
26	That is not an obstruction to the route — it is the statement that
27	
28	```
29	Pic(ℙ¹_A)  =  A[t,t⁻¹]ˣ ⧸ (A[t]ˣ · A[t⁻¹]ˣ)  =  ℤ,
30	```
31	
32	the classical computation, with the class of `t` generating.  The consequence for the
33	representability route is the useful one, and it is a *sharpening* rather than a defeat: the
34	hypothesis that must be supplied is not "all overlap units are coboundaries" but "the overlap
35	unit presenting **this** class has exponent zero" — i.e. exactly a degree-zero condition, which
36	is what `pic0Subgroup` cuts out in the first place.  A lane pricing the ring case should price
37	that, not the false universal form.
38	
39	## Where `IsDomain` is used, and where it is not
40	
41	* the **forward** direction (a coboundary is a constant) uses it, through
42	  `Polynomial.isUnit_iff` on each chart — over a general ring `A[t]` has non-constant units
43	  (`1 + εt` with `ε² = 0`) and the direction genuinely fails;
44	* the **converse** (a constant unit is a coboundary) uses **no** hypothesis on `A`: `C c` is the
45	  left chart's image of the polynomial unit `C c`.  The `omit` marker records that.
46	
47	`Algebra/LaurentUnits.lean` already proves the necessity of `IsDomain` for the Laurent unit
48	classification as a theorem rather than a remark; this file is the two-chart-cohomological
49	consequence of that classification.
50	
51	## Main declarations
52	
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.rightChart` — the second chart map `A[t] → A[t,t⁻¹]`, `t ↦ T (-1)`.  The
54	  two charts of ℙ¹ are both polynomial rings; they differ by which of `t, t⁻¹` they send `X` to.
55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.C_unit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits` — a constant unit is a coboundary, over
56	  any commutative ring.
57	* `AlgebraicGeometry.eq_C_of_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits` — over a domain, a coboundary is a
58	  constant unit.
59	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_iff` — the two together, as an `iff`.
60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.not_tUnit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits` — `t` is **not** a coboundary over a
61	  domain: the generator of `Pic(ℙ¹_A) = ℤ`, and the refutation of the universal form of the
62	  criterion's hypothesis.  `IsDomain` alone suffices — a separate `Nontrivial` binder was
63	  redundant (the `overlappingInstances` linter caught it), which is worth noting because the
64	  statement *is* false at the zero ring for the trivial reason that `t = 1` there.
65	-/
66	
67	set_option autoImplicit false
68	
69	universe u
70	
71	open CategoryTheory
72	
73	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
74	
75	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
76	
77	/-- The second ℙ¹ chart map `A[t] → A[t,t⁻¹]`, sending the coordinate to `t⁻¹`.  The first is
78	mathlib's `Polynomial.toLaurent` (`X ↦ T 1`); both chart rings are polynomial rings, and the
79	cover is recorded by *which* Laurent monomial the coordinate goes to. -/
80	noncomputable def rightChart (A : Type u) [CommRing A] :
81	    Polynomial A →+* LaurentPolynomial A :=
82	  Polynomial.eval₂RingHom LaurentPolynomial.C (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1))
83	
84	@[simp]
85	lemma rightChart_X : (rightChart A) Polynomial.X = LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) := by
86	  simp [rightChart]
87	
88	@[simp]
89	lemma rightChart_C (c : A) : (rightChart A) (Polynomial.C c) = LaurentPolynomial.C c := by
90	  simp [rightChart]
91	
92	/-- The coboundary subgroup of the ℙ¹ overlap units: products of images of the two chart unit
93	groups.  Abbreviation for the `TruncExpCech` subgroup at the two chart maps. -/
94	noncomputable abbrev laurentCoboundaryUnits (A : Type u) [CommRing A] :
95	    Subgroup (LaurentPolynomial A)ˣ :=
96	  TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits
97	    (Polynomial.toLaurent : Polynomial A →+* LaurentPolynomial A) (rightChart A)
98	
99	/-- **A constant unit is a coboundary** — no hypothesis on `A`.
100	
101	`LaurentPolynomial.C c` is the left chart's image of the polynomial unit `Polynomial.C c`. -/
102	theorem C_unit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits (c : Aˣ) :
103	    (Units.map (LaurentPolynomial.C : A →+* LaurentPolynomial A).toMonoidHom c)
104	      ∈ laurentCoboundaryUnits A := by
105	  have h : Units.map (LaurentPolynomial.C : A →+* LaurentPolynomial A).toMonoidHom c
106	      = Units.map (Polynomial.toLaurent : Polynomial A →+* LaurentPolynomial A).toMonoidHom
107	          (Units.map (Polynomial.C : A →+* Polynomial A).toMonoidHom c) := by
108	    ext; simp
109	  rw [h]
110	  exact TruncExpCech.unitsMap_mem_cechCoboundaryUnits_left _ _ _
111	
112	/-- **Over a domain, a coboundary is a constant unit.**
113	
114	Both chart unit groups consist of constants (`Polynomial.isUnit_iff`, which needs `IsDomain`),
115	and both chart maps send `Polynomial.C c` to `LaurentPolynomial.C c`, so a product of chart
116	images is `C` of the product.
117	
118	This is the direction that fails over a general ring: `1 + εt` is a unit of `A[t]` whenever
119	`ε² = 0`, so `A[t]ˣ` is bigger than the constants there. -/
120	theorem eq_C_of_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits [IsDomain A] {u : (LaurentPolynomial A)ˣ}
121	    (hu : u ∈ laurentCoboundaryUnits A) :
122	    ∃ c : A, IsUnit c ∧ (u : LaurentPolynomial A) = LaurentPolynomial.C c := by
123	  obtain ⟨v, w, hvw⟩ := TruncExpCech.mem_cechCoboundaryUnits.mp hu
124	  obtain ⟨cv, hcv, hv⟩ := Polynomial.isUnit_iff.mp v.isUnit
125	  obtain ⟨cw, hcw, hw⟩ := Polynomial.isUnit_iff.mp w.isUnit
126	  refine ⟨cv * cw, hcv.mul hcw, ?_⟩
127	  rw [← hvw]
128	  change Polynomial.toLaurent (v : Polynomial A) * (rightChart A) (w : Polynomial A)
129	    = LaurentPolynomial.C (cv * cw)
130	  rw [← hv, ← hw]
131	  simp [rightChart, map_mul]
132	
133	/-- **THE CHARACTERIZATION**: over a domain, the coboundary subgroup is exactly the constants.
134	
135	So the two-chart Čech Picard group of `ℙ¹_A` is the Laurent units modulo the constants, which by
136	`LaurentPolynomial.unitsEquiv` (`Aˣ × ℤ`) is `ℤ`. -/
137	theorem mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_iff [IsDomain A] {u : (LaurentPolynomial A)ˣ} :
138	    u ∈ laurentCoboundaryUnits A
139	      ↔ ∃ c : A, IsUnit c ∧ (u : LaurentPolynomial A) = LaurentPolynomial.C c := by
140	  refine ⟨eq_C_of_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits, ?_⟩
141	  rintro ⟨c, hc, hu⟩
142	  obtain ⟨cu, rfl⟩ := hc
143	  have h : u = Units.map (LaurentPolynomial.C : A →+* LaurentPolynomial A).toMonoidHom cu :=
144	    Units.ext hu
145	  rw [h]
146	  exact C_unit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits cu
147	
148	/-- **`t` IS NOT A COBOUNDARY** over a nontrivial domain — the generator of
149	`Pic(ℙ¹_A) = ℤ`, and the refutation of the *universal* form of the criterion's hypothesis in
150	`Picard/TwoChartCechPicTrivial.lean`.
151	
152	If it were, it would be a constant by `eq_C_of_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits`; but `T 1` has its
153	support in degree `1`, and comparing coefficients at `0` gives `0 = c` while at `1` gives
154	`1 = 0`.
155	
156	Recorded as a theorem rather than a remark because the previous file's criterion asks for *every*
157	overlap unit to be a coboundary, and a consumer must know that that hypothesis is FALSE here — so
158	the thing to supply is a degree-zero condition on the presenting unit, not the universal form. -/
159	theorem not_tUnit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits [IsDomain A] :
160	    LaurentPolynomial.tUnit (R := A) 1 ∉ laurentCoboundaryUnits A := by
161	  intro hmem
162	  obtain ⟨c, hcu, hc⟩ := eq_C_of_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits hmem
163	  rw [LaurentPolynomial.tUnit_coe] at hc
164	  -- `T 1 = C 1 * T 1` and `C c = C c * T 0`, so `exp_unique` gives `1 = 0`
165	  have h : (LaurentPolynomial.C (1 : A) * LaurentPolynomial.T (1 : ℤ))
166	      = LaurentPolynomial.C c * LaurentPolynomial.T (0 : ℤ) := by
167	    rw [map_one, one_mul, LaurentPolynomial.T_zero, mul_one]
168	    exact hc
169	  exact absurd (LaurentPolynomial.exp_unique (one_ne_zero (α := A)) h) one_ne_zero
170	
171	end AlgebraicGeometry

1	/-

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorDatumRankOne
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0VanishingFieldTest
8	
9	/-!
10	# THE RIGID ENGINE FIRES AT GENUS `0` ON A FIBREWISE-TRIVIAL CLASS, OVER A TEST RING
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0VanishingFieldTest.lean` closed every **field** instance of the degree-zero
13	Picard vanishing at genus `0`; `Picard/Pic0VanishingAffineReduction.lean` proved the `∀ T`
14	binder *is* the `∀` test-ring binder.  What remained was the **ring** case, and the note
15	released with it priced that as "cohomology and base change, absent from this tree".
16	
17	**That price was wrong, and this file is the correction.**  The relevant engine is landed and
18	is stated over an arbitrary test ring for an arbitrary class:
19	
20	* `Cohomology/GluedSheafExtraction.lean:301` — every Čech Picard class on `C_B` is
21	  `D.cechPicClass` for some `BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π`, at **every** `k`-algebra `B`;
22	* `Cohomology/GluedSheafEngine.lean:198` — `datumRigidEngine`: from a *fibrewise* `H¹`
23	  hypothesis, `H¹(C_B, F_D) = 0` and `H⁰(C_B, F_D)` is finite projective over `B`;
24	* `Cohomology/GluedSheafDatumFibre.lean:169` — the fibrewise hypothesis follows from a
25	  witness divisor on the fibre curve with vanishing `H¹`;
26	* `Picard/DivisorDatumRankOne.lean:148` — on the vanishing locus, at fibre degree `n` and
27	  `χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n`, the stalk rank of `H⁰` is `1`.
28	
29	What nobody had connected is that at **genus `0`** the fibre inputs of that chain are *free*
30	rather than expensive, and this file proves exactly that.
31	
32	## The two results, and why the hypothesis is the cheap one
33	
34	The fibre witness is the **zero divisor**.  Its class is `1` (`picClass_zero`) and its sheaf is
35	the structure sheaf (`moduleKSheafDivisorSheafZeroIso`), whose `H¹` has `K`-dimension
36	`genus C` at every field extension `K/k` (`finrank_h1_baseField_eq_genus`) — so at genus `0` it
37	vanishes, at every prime of `B` at once, with no locus, no openness argument and no
38	spreading-out.  Hence:
39	
40	* `subsingleton_h1_residueField_tensor_of_genus_zero` — the engine's `hfib` clause, for **any**
41	  datum whose fibre classes are trivial;
42	* `rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_genus_zero` — `H⁰` of stalk rank `1` at every prime,
43	  i.e. `π_*L` invertible in the rank spelling, with `χ = 1` supplied by `genus C = 0` rather
44	  than assumed.
45	
46	**The hypothesis is fibre-class triviality, not fibre degree.**  That spelling is deliberate
47	and is not a strengthening in disguise: at genus `0` the two are *equivalent* by the landed
48	field-level converse (`eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_chi_one`), and
49	`fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` below is that equivalence at this site.  The
50	reason to state the theorems on triviality is mechanical, and worth recording because it will
51	bite the next lane: `classDeg K` carries five instance binders on the fibre curve
52	(`IsIntegral`, `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1`, `QuasiCompact`, and both `Module.Finite`
53	Betti-number clauses) which do not synthesize through the `relCurve` `def` barrier, so a
54	hypothesis phrased `∀ p, classDeg κ(p) … = 0` **cannot be stated** at a general prime without
55	`haveI`-installing them first — measured, not guessed.  Triviality of the class needs none of
56	them.
57	
58	## What this does NOT do
59	
60	* **It does not discharge the `pic⁰` vanishing at a test ring.**  It supplies the two
61	  cohomological outputs — `H¹ = 0` and `H⁰` invertible — that the classical proof consumes
62	  next through the evaluation map `π^*π_*L → L`.
63	
64	  **CORRECTED after a fresh-context audit (`I-1651`).**  An earlier version of this bullet said
65	  that map "does not exist in this tree, in the sibling project, or in mathlib (measured this
66	  session)".  **The mathlib half was false and unmeasured**: the map is the counit of
67	  `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction`
68	  (`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Modules/Sheaf.lean`), and the sibling project applies
69	  `.counit.app` to it in two files.  What is genuinely absent is any theorem saying that counit
70	  is an **isomorphism** at a sheaf of this kind — that is the real residue, and it is a
71	  narrower and more defensible claim than the one this bullet used to make.  AJCR's own
72	  carriers are `Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (ModuleCat R)`, not `Scheme.Modules`, so
73	  reaching the counit here is itself a port.
74	* **It says nothing at positive genus**, where the fibre `H¹` is genuinely nonzero and the
75	  witness above fails at the first step.
76	* It introduces **no hypothesis on the curve** beyond the three standing binders and
77	  `genus C = 0`, and no hypothesis on the test ring beyond `IsNoetherianRing` — which
78	  `Cohomology/DatumDescent.lean:547` is designed to remove and which a consumer should remove
79	  through that route rather than by re-proving anything here.
80	
81	## Main declarations
82	
83	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.subsingleton_h1_residueField_tensor_of_genus_zero`
84	  — **the engine's fibrewise hypothesis, free at genus `0`**.
85	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rigidEngine_of_genus_zero` — the engine's three
86	  conclusions with the fibrewise clause discharged.
87	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_genus_zero` —
88	  **`H⁰` of stalk rank `1`**, at every prime.
89	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` — the
90	  degree-`0` spelling of the hypothesis implies the triviality spelling, so nothing is lost by
91	  stating the results on the latter.
92	-/
93	
94	set_option autoImplicit false
95	
96	universe u
97	
98	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory TensorProduct
99	
100	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
101	
102	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
103	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
104	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
105	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
106	
107	noncomputable section
108	
109	namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum
110	
111	/-! ## The fibre inputs at genus `0` -/
112	
113	/-- **`H¹` of the structure sheaf of the fibre curve vanishes at genus `0`**, at every field
114	extension of the base.
115	
116	`finrank_h1_baseField_eq_genus` computes that dimension as `genus C` on the nose, so this is
117	the hypothesis read as a dimension count; the `Module.Free` instance the `finrank` criterion
118	wants is the vector-space one. -/
119	theorem subsingleton_h1_moduleKSheaf_baseChange_of_genus_zero (hg : genus C = 0)
120	    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] :
121	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.moduleKSheaf K) 1) := by
122	  have h : Module.finrank K
123	      (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.moduleKSheaf K) 1) = genus C :=
124	    finrank_h1_baseField_eq_genus C K
125	  rw [hg] at h
126	  exact (Module.finrank_eq_zero_iff_of_free _ _).mp h
127	
128	/-- **The zero divisor is a vanishing witness at genus `0`**: `H¹(𝒪(0)) = H¹(𝒪) = 0`.
129	
130	`moduleKSheafDivisorSheafZeroIso` is the identification of the two sheaves; the transport is
131	`Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv`. -/
132	theorem subsingleton_h1_divisorSheaf_zero_of_genus_zero (hg : genus C = 0)
133	    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] :
134	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.divisorSheaf K
135	      (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.CurveDivisor)) 1) :=
136	  (Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv (Scheme.moduleKSheafDivisorSheafZeroIso
137	    (X := (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left) K) 1).toEquiv.subsingleton_congr.mp
138	      (subsingleton_h1_moduleKSheaf_baseChange_of_genus_zero hg K)
139	
140	/-- **THE ENGINE'S FIBREWISE HYPOTHESIS, FREE AT GENUS `0`**: for a datum whose fibre class at
141	the prime `p` is trivial, the complex-form clause `hfib p` of `datumRigidEngine` holds.
142	
143	The witness fed to `subsingleton_h1_residueField_tensor_of_witness` is the **zero divisor**:
144	its class is `1` by `picClass_zero`, which is the fibre class by hypothesis, and its `H¹`
145	vanishes by the lemma above.  No locus, no openness, no spreading-out, and the argument is
146	uniform in `p`. -/
147	theorem subsingleton_h1_residueField_tensor_of_genus_zero
148	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hg : genus C = 0) (p : PrimeSpectrum B)
149	    (htriv : (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1) :
150	    Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
151	  refine D.subsingleton_h1_residueField_tensor_of_witness p ⟨0, ?_, ?_⟩
152	  · rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_zero, htriv]
153	    rfl
154	  · exact subsingleton_h1_divisorSheaf_zero_of_genus_zero hg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
155	
156	/-! ## The engine, and the rank-`1` export -/
157	
158	/-- **The rigid engine at genus `0` on a fibrewise-trivial class**: `H¹(C_B, F_D) = 0` and
159	`H⁰(C_B, F_D)` finite projective over `B`, with the fibrewise clause discharged by the
160	genus hypothesis rather than assumed. -/
161	theorem rigidEngine_of_genus_zero (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) [IsNoetherianRing B]
162	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) (hg : genus C = 0)
163	    (htriv : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B,
164	      (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1) :
165	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 1) ∧
166	      Module.Finite B (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) ∧
167	      Module.Projective B (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) :=
168	  datumRigidEngine D hπ fun p =>
169	    D.subsingleton_h1_residueField_tensor_of_genus_zero hg p (htriv p)
170	
171	/-- **`H⁰` HAS STALK RANK `1` AT EVERY PRIME** — `π_*L` invertible, in the rank spelling, for a
172	fibrewise-trivial class on a genus-`0` curve over an arbitrary Noetherian test ring.
173	
174	`rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one` is applied at `n := 0`: its χ-normalization
175	`χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n` is `χ = 1`, which `chi_moduleKSheaf` plus `genus C = 0` supplies, and its
176	fibre-degree clause is `classDeg κ(p) 1 = 0`, which is `classDeg_one`.  The five fibre
177	instances are installed by hand — they do not synthesize through the `relCurve` `def`
178	barrier. -/
179	theorem rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_genus_zero
180	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) [IsNoetherianRing B]
181	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) (hg : genus C = 0)
182	    (htriv : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B,
183	      (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1)
184	    (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
185	    Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1 := by
186	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
187	    instIsIntegralBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
188	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
189	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
190	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
191	  haveI : QuasiCompact
192	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
193	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
194	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule
195	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0) :=
196	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
197	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule
198	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1) :=
199	    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
200	  refine D.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one (n := 0) hπ ?_
201	    (fun q => D.subsingleton_h1_residueField_tensor_of_genus_zero hg q (htriv q)) p ?_
202	  · rw [chi_moduleKSheaf C, hg]
203	  · rw [htriv p, Nat.cast_zero]
204	    exact classDeg_one _

206	/-! ## The degree spelling is the same hypothesis at genus `0` -/
207	
208	/-- **The degree-`0` spelling implies the triviality spelling**, at genus `0`: a fibre class of
209	degree `0` *is* trivial, by the landed field-level converse
210	`eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_chi_one` at `χ = 1`.
211	
212	So the theorems above lose no generality by taking triviality as the hypothesis; what they
213	gain is that the hypothesis is statable without the five fibre instances `classDeg` needs.
214	Consumers holding a degree hypothesis at a prime pass through here. -/
215	theorem fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero
216	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hg : genus C = 0) (p : PrimeSpectrum B)
217	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField)]
218	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
219	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
220	    [QuasiCompact
221	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
222	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule
223	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0)]
224	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule
225	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1)]
226	    (hdeg : classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
227	      (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 0) :
228	    (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1 :=
229	  eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_chi_one p.asIdeal.ResidueField
230	    (chi_moduleKSheaf_baseChange_eq_one_of_genus_zero C p.asIdeal.ResidueField hg) _ hdeg
231	
232	end BasicOpenCocycleDatum

7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.LaurentCoboundaryReduced
8	
9	/-!
10	# THE ℙ¹ TWO-CHART COBOUNDARY SUBGROUP OVER AN ARBITRARY RING
11	
12	Assembling the three landed pieces, the ℙ¹ two-chart coboundary subgroup `laurentCoboundaryUnits A`
13	is now characterised over an **arbitrary** commutative ring — no domain, reducedness, or field
14	hypothesis:
15	
16	> a Laurent unit is a coboundary **iff** it is `C c · (1 + z)` for a unit `c` of `A` and a
17	> **nilpotent** Laurent polynomial `z`.
18	
19	Equivalently: the coboundary subgroup is exactly the **exponent-zero** units — those with no
20	`T`-degree, i.e. a constant unit deformed by a nilpotent.  This is `Pic(ℙ¹_A) = ℤ` in the sharp
21	form that survives base change to a non-reduced ring: the class of a Laurent unit is its exponent,
22	and a unit presents the trivial class iff its exponent is `0`.
23	
24	The two directions:
25	
26	* **forward** (a coboundary is `C c · (1 + z)`): `eq_C_mul_one_add_nilpotent_of_mem_…`
27	  (`Algebra/LaurentCoboundaryReduced.lean`) — a product of chart units is a constant times a
28	  unipotent;
29	* **backward** (`C c · (1 + z)` is a coboundary): `C c` is a coboundary
30	  (`C_unit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits`) and `1 + z` is a coboundary for nilpotent `z`
31	  (`nilpotent_one_add_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits`), and coboundaries are a subgroup.
32	
33	## Main declarations
34	
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.C_mul_one_add_nilpotent_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits` — the backward direction.
36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_iff_general` — the arbitrary-ring characterisation.
37	-/
38	
39	set_option autoImplicit false
40	
41	universe u
42	
43	open CategoryTheory LaurentPolynomial
44	
45	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
46	
47	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
48	
49	/-- **`C c · (1 + z)` is a coboundary** for a unit `c` and a nilpotent Laurent polynomial `z`.
50	
51	`C c` is a coboundary (`C_unit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits`), `1 + z` is a coboundary
52	(`nilpotent_one_add_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits`), and coboundaries form a subgroup. -/
53	theorem C_mul_one_add_nilpotent_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits {c : A} (hc : IsUnit c)
54	    {z : LaurentPolynomial A} (hz : IsNilpotent z) (u : (LaurentPolynomial A)ˣ)
55	    (hu : (u : LaurentPolynomial A) = LaurentPolynomial.C c * (1 + z)) :
56	    u ∈ laurentCoboundaryUnits A := by
57	  obtain ⟨cu, rfl⟩ := hc
58	  have hzu : IsUnit (1 + z) := hz.isUnit_one_add
59	  have hfact : u = (Units.map (LaurentPolynomial.C : A →+* LaurentPolynomial A).toMonoidHom cu)
60	      * hzu.unit := by
61	    apply Units.ext
62	    rw [hu]; simp [Units.coe_map]
63	  rw [hfact]
64	  exact Subgroup.mul_mem _ (C_unit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits cu)
65	    (nilpotent_one_add_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits hz hzu.unit rfl)
66	
67	/-- **THE ARBITRARY-RING CHARACTERISATION**: a Laurent unit is a two-chart coboundary **iff** it
68	is `C c · (1 + z)` for a unit `c` and a nilpotent `z` — a constant unit times a unipotent, i.e.
69	exponent zero.  Holds over an arbitrary commutative ring, with no domain, reducedness, or field
70	hypothesis. -/
71	theorem mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_iff_general {u : (LaurentPolynomial A)ˣ} :
72	    u ∈ laurentCoboundaryUnits A
73	      ↔ ∃ (c : A) (z : LaurentPolynomial A), IsUnit c ∧ IsNilpotent z ∧
74	          (u : LaurentPolynomial A) = LaurentPolynomial.C c * (1 + z) := by
75	  refine ⟨eq_C_mul_one_add_nilpotent_of_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits, ?_⟩
76	  rintro ⟨c, z, hc, hz, hu⟩
77	  exact C_mul_one_add_nilpotent_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits hc hz u hu
78	
79	end AlgebraicGeometry

8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafExtraction
9	
10	/-!
11	# THE RIGID ENGINE FIRES FROM A `pic⁰` MEMBERSHIP, WITH NO FIBREWISE BINDER LEFT
12	
13	`Picard/Pic0RingDatumEngine.lean` fires the RE-4 rigid engine at genus `0` on a
14	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π` under the fibrewise binder
15	
16	  `htriv : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B, (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1`
17	
18	and `Picard/Pic0RingFibrewiseTrivial.lean` proves the corresponding statement for a class in
19	`pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B)`.  **This file joins the two**: for a cocycle-presented `pic⁰`
20	class the binder is discharged, so the engine's conclusions hold with no fibrewise hypothesis
21	anywhere in the statement.
22	
23	## What had to be written, and why it is not a restatement
24	
25	Three spelling seams, each of which had to be crossed rather than asserted:
26	
27	1. **`relCurveMap` vs the whiskering.**  The engine's base-change naturality
28	   (`cechPicClass_baseChange`) is stated on `relCurveMap C B B'`, which is *defined* as
29	   `(C ◁ overSpecMap B B').left` (`Cohomology/RelativeSectionsLinear.lean:160`); the degree
30	   seam (`Picard/DegreeSeam.lean:81`) is stated on `(C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left`.  The two
31	   `overSpecMap`s are **independent definitions in different namespaces** — the duplicate pair
32	   recorded as `I-0144` — and they agree by `rfl` only when `φ` is the canonical algebra map
33	   `(Algebra.ofId B κ(p)).restrictScalars k`.  `relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField` is
34	   that identification, and everything downstream needs it.
35	2. **Field points vs primes.**  `pic0Subgroup` membership quantifies over `k`-algebra maps
36	   into fields; the engine quantifies over `PrimeSpectrum B`.  A residue field *is* such a
37	   field but the instantiation is a written step, not an observation.
38	3. **Degree vs triviality.**  What the membership gives at a prime is a vanishing `classDeg`;
39	   what the engine wants is a trivial class.  The engine's own
40	   `fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` converts one to the other at genus `0`, and
41	   it carries **five fibre instance binders** that do not synthesize through the `relCurve`
42	   `def` barrier; they are installed by hand here, as they are there.
43	
44	## What this buys, stated exactly
45	
46	The remaining distance from a `pic⁰` class over a test ring to *triviality* of that class is
47	now: `H¹(C_B, F) = 0` and `H⁰(C_B, F)` invertible (stalk rank `1` at every prime) **are
48	available**, unconditionally on the class beyond its being degree-zero and presented.  On the
49	**divisor/pushforward route** the step that turns an invertible pushforward into a
50	trivialization of the class is the evaluation map `π^*π_*L → L`, which my search did not find in
51	this tree.
52	
53	**Scope corrected after review.**  An earlier version of this paragraph called that evaluation
54	map "the remaining step" for the ring case as such, and asserted its absence from the sibling
55	project and mathlib as measured.  Both were too strong.  It is the remaining step on *this*
56	route only: `Picard/Pic0VanishingRigidityReduction.lean` reaches the same vanishing through
57	field-point rigidity, which never produces a divisor and so never needs the evaluation map at
58	all.  And I verified absence only in AJCR — not in `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge`, which has
59	adjunction/counit material, and not in mathlib.
60	
61	## What this does NOT do
62	
63	* **It does not prove the ring case**, and it is not on the shortest route to it.  The
64	  evaluation step above is not built here; a fibrewise-trivial class over a ring need not be
65	  trivial (Traverso–Swan: `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic (Polynomial A))` fails even *given*
66	  `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic A)`, measured).  A lane wanting only the vanishing should read
67	  `Pic0VanishingRigidityReduction.lean` first: it reduces the same goal to field-point rigidity
68	  with no cohomology, no pushforward and no divisor.  What *this* file is for is the
69	  pushforward route, where `π_*L` invertible is the object of interest in its own right.
70	* **`IsNoetherianRing B` is inherited**, not introduced: it is the engine's own binder, which
71	  `Cohomology/DatumDescent.lean:547` is designed to remove.  Nothing here re-proves it and a
72	  consumer should remove it through that route.
73	* **The cocycle presentation is a real hypothesis** on the `pic⁰` class, inherited from the
74	  DAT-4 degree seam.  `exists_cechPicClass_eq` produces a datum for any Čech class on `C_B`,
75	  but relating *that* datum's class to the plus-class presentation of a `picEt` element is the
76	  `picEtAffineEquiv`/`unit` seam, and it is assumed here rather than proved.
77	
78	  **What the binder is, exactly, after measurement — and a first answer CORRECTED.**  The
79	  *datum* half is free: `exists_datum_pic0_presentation` below produces a presenting datum for
80	  any class whose affine collapse is `PicEtAff.unit` of *some* relative class (`relPicMk` is
81	  surjective and `exists_cechPicClass_eq` is total over every `k`-algebra).
82	
83	  An earlier version of this paragraph then named ring-level surjectivity of `PicEtAff.unit` as
84	  the remaining brick, on the ground that `PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section`
85	  (`Picard/EffectivityClose.lean:141`) is field-only and section-dependent.  **That was wrong**,
86	  and a fresh-context audit caught it: `picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt`
87	  (`Picard/PicEtUnit.lean:161`) supplies the seam at an **arbitrary test ring**, with no field,
88	  no section and no curve hypothesis, for every class in the range of `relPicToPicEt`.  So the
89	  seam is not the obstruction it was priced as; `presentation_of_relPicToPicEt` below is that
90	  observation made usable, and `rigidEngine_of_relPicToPicEt` fires the engine with the
91	  presentation binder **eliminated** for such classes.
92	
93	  What is genuinely missing is therefore **surjectivity of `relPicToPicEt` onto `picEt`** — that
94	  every étale-plus class over a ring comes from a relative Picard class — which is a different
95	  statement about a different map, and is what a lane wanting these conclusions at an
96	  *arbitrary* degree-zero class should target.  `Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:199` calls
97	  membership in that range "honesty" and treats it as a real condition, which is consistent.
98	* **Genus `0` only.**  At positive genus the fibre classes are not trivial.
99	
100	## Main declarations
101	
102	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField` — the `I-0144` spelling bridge.
103	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_datum_relPicMk_eq` / `exists_datum_pic0_presentation` — the datum in
104	  the presentation binder is produced, not assumed, at every test ring.
105	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.htriv_of_pic0` — **the discharge**: the engine's
106	  fibrewise binder, from a cocycle-presented `pic⁰` class.
107	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rigidEngine_of_pic0` — the engine's three
108	  conclusions with no fibrewise hypothesis.
109	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0` —
110	  **`π_*L` invertible** from a `pic⁰` membership.
111	* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0` — non-vacuity at `ℙ¹` over an
112	  arbitrary field.
113	-/
114	
115	set_option autoImplicit false
116	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
117	
118	universe u
119	
120	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite

## Report: the `pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)` route and the seminormality obstruction

All paths below are under `/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/`. All the key files checked are sorry-free; `PicEtAff.unit_injective` is proved (C1 étale-separatedness), not gated on an axiom.

### (a) The exact map chain: `CechPic → relPic → PicEtAff → picEt → pic0Subgroup`

For `X = (C ⊗ overSpec k A).left` (the base-changed curve) and affine test `T = overSpec k A`:

1. **`Scheme.CechPic X`** — `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic.lean:60`. The *Zariski* Čech `H¹(X, 𝒪ˣ)`, a `Quotient` over all pointed covers stabilised under refinement (so it is the full Picard group, seeing every cover, not just two-chart ones).

2. **`relPic C T := CechPic((C⊗T).left) ⧸ picFromBase C T`** — `RelPic.lean:54,63-64`. `picFromBase` = range of pullback from the base `T` (`RelPic.lean:54`). Projection `relPicMk` at `RelPic.lean:70`; restriction `relPicAlgMap C f := relPicMap C (overSpecMap f)` at `RelPicAlgebra.lean:88-90`.

3. **`PicEtAff C A`** — `PicEtAff.lean:218`. The **one-step étale plus construction** of `relPic`: `Quotient` of `Σ (E : EtaleCover A), descentClasses C E` modulo agreement on a common refinement (`descentClasses` = equalizer of the two `relPicAlgMap`s of the double-cover projections, `PicEtAff.lean:76-80`). The **unit** `relPic C (overSpec k A) →* PicEtAff C A` is at `PicEtAff.lean:377`, and it is **INJECTIVE** — `PicEtAff.unit_injective`, `CechKernelLemma.lean:361` (Kleiman 2.5(1), "axiom C1", but proved sorry-free here). This is decisive for part (b): the plus does **not** collapse `relPic` classes.

4. **`picEt C T`** — `PicEt.lean:105`. The bespoke affine-opens limit: the subgroup of `∏_{U ∈ T.left.affineOpens} PicEtAff C Γ(T.left,U)` cut out by restriction-compatibility.

5. **`picEtAffineEquiv C A : picEt C (overSpec k A) ≃* PicEtAff C A`** — `PicEt.lean:235` (limit collapses at the terminal `⊤` of an affine test's affine-opens poset). **So for an affine test, `picEt` IS `PicEtAff` — YES to your question.**

6. **`pic0Subgroup C T`** — `Pic0Functor.lean:107`. Subgroup of `picEt C T` of classes with `degAt lam t = 0` at *every* field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`. `degAt` (`Pic0Functor.lean:54`) restricts `lam` along `t`, collapses via `picEtAffineEquiv C K` to `PicEtAff C K`, and takes `PicEtAff.degAff`.

Note: **`relPicMulEquivCechPic` (`RelPicPointTest.lean:99`) is NOT on this chain for general `A`.** It requires `[Subsingleton T.left]` (a one-point test) and is a Wave-5 dual-numbers tool. For `overSpec k A` with `A` a general ring, `Spec A` has many points, so it does not apply.

So `PicEtAff C A` is the **étale sheafification** of the relative Picard group `relPic C (overSpec k A) = CechPic(ℙ¹_A) / (pullbacks from Spec A)` — with an injective unit from `relPic`. It is *not* the absolute `CommRing.Pic(A[t])`; it is the relative Picard, étale-plus'd.

### (b) Verdict: the seminormality obstruction DOES bite the `pic0Subgroup` route (it is not confined to a naive `CommRing.Pic` route)

The étale/plus construction does **not** sheafify away the `Pic(A[t])` contribution. Three concrete reasons, each with evidence:

1. **The plus unit is injective (`CechKernelLemma.lean:361`).** `relPic C (overSpec k A) ↪ PicEtAff C A`. So every nonzero class of `relPic` survives into `PicEtAff = picEt`. The plus can only *add* étale-local classes, never collapse `relPic` ones. Hence it cannot kill a nonzero `relPic` class.

2. **Étale sheafification leaves `Pic` unchanged** (line bundles satisfy étale descent). The Traverso–Swan classes in `Pic(A[t])/Pic(A)` for non-seminormal `A` are genuine line bundles, not étale-locally-trivial phantoms, so étale-sheafifying does not remove them.

3. **The landed Laurent theory only resolves the two-chart / chart-trivial layer.** `mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_iff_general` (`Algebra/LaurentCoboundaryGeneral.lean:71`) computes, over an arbitrary ring, that the two-chart coboundary subgroup = exponent-zero units (`C c·(1+z)`, `c` unit, `z` nilpotent) — i.e. the *two-chart* relative Čech `H¹` of `ℙ¹_A` is `ℤ` (degree), even non-reduced. But the criterion consuming it, `Scheme.cechPic_eq_one_of_forall_presenting_coboundary` (`TwoChartCechPicTrivial.lean:151`), has a **chart-triviality hypothesis** `hL : ∀ s, CechPic.map (V s).ι L = 1` — the class must already be trivial on each chart `A[t]`, `A[t⁻¹]`. Classes coming from `Pic(A[t])/Pic(A)` (nonzero exactly for non-seminormal `A`) are **not** chart-trivial and live in finer covers, invisible to the two-chart Čech `H¹`. So the Laurent bridge cannot touch them.

Consequence: a Traverso–Swan class (fibrewise-trivial, degree-zero, nonzero line bundle on `ℙ¹_A` for non-seminormal `A`) is a nonzero element of `relPic`, hence — by injectivity of the unit — nonzero in `picEt`, and since it is fibrewise trivial its `degAt` vanishes at every field point (this is exactly what `pic0_fibre_eq_one_of_genus_zero`, `Pic0RingFibrewiseTrivial.lean:141`, records). It is therefore a would-be **nonzero member of `pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)`**. So the obstruction is on the `pic0Subgroup` route itself, not merely on a naive `CommRing.Pic(A[t])` route.

The lane's own docstrings corroborate this and never claim the plus/étale layer resolves it: `P1DegreeZeroTrivial.lean:70-84`, `Pic0RingFibrewiseTrivial.lean:89-93`, `Pic0RingZariskiLocal.lean:111-119`, and `Pic0RingEngineFromPic0.lean:63-69` all state that `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic (Polynomial A))` fails even given `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic A)`, citing Traverso–Swan, and treat the ring case as genuinely open. Either way, the seminormality content is live and unaddressed on this route. This is the crux the lane must confront: it must either restrict to seminormal/reduced `A`, or prove a genuine "fibrewise-trivial ⟹ trivial" rigidity (cohomology-and-base-change) that does not exist in the tree.

### Bottom line

The field case is closed (`Pic0VanishingFieldTest.lean`, sorry-free) because `Pic(K[t]) = 0`. Everything for the ring case is either a *quantifier reduction that is provably not a weakening* (file #2), a *cohomological half-result missing the counit-iso* (files #3–4), or a *complete pure-algebra layer with no scheme-level bridge and a chart-triviality wall* (file #5). The single mathematical fact blocking all of them is the same: fibrewise-trivial ⇏ trivial for line bundles on `ℙ¹_A` over non-seminormal `A` (Traverso–Swan).
